plain.en: a to-and-fro movement, repeated again and again

means.en: Sound is produced by vibration. One to-and-fro movement is called an oscillation.

plain.en: the object that vibrates and makes the sound

means.en: The object that vibrates and makes a sound, such as a plucked rubber band or a struck tuning fork.

plain.en: one complete to-and-fro movement

means.en: One complete to-and-fro movement. A vibration is many oscillations, one after another.

plain.en: two stretched flaps in your voice box that vibrate when you speak

means.en: Two tightly stretched muscular flaps in the larynx. Air from the lungs makes them vibrate when you speak or sing.

plain.en: your voice box

means.en: The voice box in your throat. It holds the two vocal cords.

plain.en: the material that sound travels through

means.en: The material that sound travels through: a solid, a liquid or a gas. A vacuum has no medium, so sound cannot travel through it.

plain.en: a space with no matter in it

means.en: A space with no matter in it at all. Sound cannot travel through a vacuum, because there is no medium.

plain.en: a region packed closer than average

means.en: The region of a sound wave where the particles are packed closer together than average, so the density is higher than average.

plain.en: a region more spread out than average

means.en: The region of a sound wave where the particles are more spread out than average, so the density is lower than average.

plain.en: how closely the particles are packed

means.en: How closely the particles of a medium are packed together. In a sound wave, the density goes above and below the average.

plain.en: compressions and rarefactions travelling through a medium

means.en: A series of compressions and rarefactions travelling through a medium, while each particle only vibrates about its own place.

plain.en: a wave that needs matter in order to travel

means.en: A wave that needs a medium to travel. Sound is a mechanical wave, so it cannot travel through a vacuum.

plain.en: particles vibrate parallel to the way the wave travels

means.en: A wave in which the particles vibrate along the direction the wave travels. Sound in air is a longitudinal wave.

plain.en: particles vibrate at right angles to the way the wave travels

means.en: A wave in which the particles vibrate at right angles to the direction the wave travels, like a rope shaken up and down.

plain.en: the distance from one crest to the next

means.en: The distance from one crest to the next, or from one trough to the next, written λ.

plain.en: the number of oscillations per second at a fixed place

means.en: The number of oscillations per second at a fixed place, written ν. It is measured in hertz (Hz).

plain.en: the unit of frequency: one oscillation per second

means.en: The unit of frequency. One hertz (Hz) is one oscillation per second.

plain.en: the time one oscillation takes

means.en: The time for one complete oscillation at a fixed place, written T. Frequency = 1 ÷ T.

plain.en: the highest point of a density graph, under a compression

means.en: The highest point of a density graph. It sits under a compression, where the density is highest.

plain.en: the lowest point of a density graph, under a rarefaction

means.en: The lowest point of a density graph. It sits under a rarefaction, where the density is lowest.

plain.en: the biggest change in density from the average

means.en: The biggest change in density from the average, in a compression or a rarefaction. A larger amplitude carries more energy.

plain.en: sound energy through one unit area each second

means.en: The amount of sound energy that passes through one unit area, facing the sound, in one second. It falls as you move away from the source.

plain.en: how high or low a sound is; it goes with frequency

means.en: How high or low a sound is. A higher frequency gives a higher pitch.

plain.en: how loud a sound seems; it goes with amplitude

means.en: How loud a sound seems. A larger amplitude sounds louder. It also depends on the listener's hearing.

plain.en: the quality that makes two instruments sound different on the same note

means.en: The quality that makes two instruments sound different on the same note. It comes from their overtones.

plain.en: below 20 Hz, too low for humans to hear

means.en: Sound below 20 Hz. Humans cannot hear it, but elephants can detect it. It is used to detect earthquakes.

plain.en: above 20 kHz, too high for humans to hear

means.en: Sound above 20 kHz. Humans cannot hear it, but dogs, bats and dolphins can. It is used in ultrasonography and sonar.

plain.en: the frequencies humans can hear: about 20 Hz to 20 kHz

means.en: The range of frequencies that humans can hear, from about 20 Hz to 20 000 Hz. It narrows with age.

plain.en: a unit often used for loudness

means.en: Loudness is often measured in decibels (dB). Normal talk is about 60 dB.

plain.en: unwanted or harmful sound

means.en: Unwanted or harmful sound. Long exposure to loud sound can cause hearing loss.

plain.en: a thin membrane in the ear that vibrates when sound arrives

means.en: A thin membrane at the end of the ear canal. Sound makes it vibrate, and tiny bones pass the vibration on.

plain.en: the part of the ear that turns vibrations into signals for the brain

means.en: The part of the inner ear that turns vibrations into electrical signals, which travel to the brain.

plain.en: a sound of a single frequency

means.en: A sound of a single frequency, like the sound of a tuning fork.

plain.en: the lowest frequency in a note

means.en: The lowest frequency in a note.

plain.en: a higher frequency in a note, above the fundamental

means.en: The higher frequencies in a note, above the fundamental. They give an instrument its timbre.

plain.en: two notes where one has double the frequency of the other

means.en: Two notes are an octave apart when one has double the frequency of the other, such as 200 Hz and 400 Hz.

plain.en: sound bouncing off an obstacle

means.en: Sound bouncing off a surface. The incoming sound and the reflected sound make equal angles with the normal.

plain.en: a reflected sound heard separately, at least 0.1 s later

means.en: A reflected sound heard separately from the original sound. It must reach you at least 0.1 s after the original.

plain.en: sound that goes on after the source stops, from many reflections

means.en: Sound that goes on after the source stops, because of many reflections off the walls, ceiling and floor.

plain.en: finding objects using reflected sound

means.en: Finding objects using reflected sound. Bats send out bursts of ultrasound and sense the echoes.

plain.en: sound navigation and ranging

means.en: Sound navigation and ranging. A ship sends ultrasound into the water and uses the echoes to find underwater objects.
